nodes.name: config.go
nodes.summary: Defines the full ServerConfig schema (brokers, SEMP client settings, Hop 1/Hop 2 auth, observability) and implements loading from YAML with ${VAR} env substitution, defaulting, and exhaustive validation.

nodes.name: selectedMethod
nodes.summary: Inspects which BrokerClientAuth sub-block is populated and returns its method name when exactly one is set, else returns structural validation errors.

nodes.name: allowedClientAuthMethods
nodes.summary: Returns every OAuth client-auth method name the schema currently supports, for use in operator-facing error messages.

nodes.name: LogValue
nodes.summary: Implements slog.LogValuer for BrokerOAuthConfig, exposing non-secret IdP coordinates and the resolved auth method while excluding credential material.

nodes.name: Broker
nodes.summary: Looks up a broker's config by alias, compared case-insensitively against the canonicalized broker map.

nodes.name: BrokerAliases
nodes.summary: Returns the configured broker aliases in their original display casing, sorted alphabetically.

nodes.name: Hop2OAuthActive
nodes.summary: Reports whether the Hop-2 (server-to-broker) OAuth token-exchange runtime should be constructed: requires both a populated broker_oauth block and at least one broker in oauth mode.

nodes.name: DisplayName
nodes.summary: Returns the broker alias in its original YAML casing for use in logs and user-facing output.

nodes.name: Load
nodes.summary: Locates the server config file by trying CONFIG_FILE, then the system path, then the local dev path in order, and loads it via LoadConfig.

nodes.name: sanitizeYAMLError
nodes.summary: Strips backtick-quoted raw node values from a YAML decode error so a credential pulled into a mismatched field cannot leak through the error string.

nodes.name: ReadResolvedConfigFile
nodes.summary: Performs the read, .env-load, and ${VAR} substitution steps of config loading without parsing/validating, so partial readers like the health probe see identical resolved bytes to the server.

nodes.name: LoadConfig
nodes.summary: Reads, resolves env vars, parses, defaults, applies env overrides, and validates a YAML config file into a ready ServerConfig.

nodes.name: applyDefaults
nodes.summary: Fills every optional ServerConfig field left unset with its shipped default, including loopback-only binding outside OAuth mode and tool-authorization/observability sub-defaults.

nodes.name: loadEnvFile
nodes.summary: Loads a .env file (from ENV_FILE or alongside the config file) into the process environment without overwriting variables already set.

nodes.name: stripMatchedQuotes
nodes.summary: Removes one matching pair of surrounding double or single quotes from a .env value.

nodes.name: isValidAlias
nodes.summary: Checks a broker alias against the 1-63 char, alphanumeric-with-hyphens contract.

nodes.name: validateAndCanonicalizeBrokers
nodes.summary: Validates broker alias syntax and case-insensitive uniqueness, then rewrites the broker map to canonical lowercase keys while preserving original display casing.

nodes.name: substituteEnvVars
nodes.summary: Replaces every ${VAR_NAME} reference in raw YAML bytes with its environment value outside of whole-line and inline comments, erroring on an unset variable.

nodes.name: splitYAMLComment
nodes.summary: Splits a YAML line into its content and trailing comment, respecting quoted strings so a '#' inside a quoted value is not treated as a comment start.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Runs the full ServerConfig validation pass: required fields, auth mode rules, TLS pairing and production-mode guardrails, broker checks, and tool-authorization consistency, collecting and returning every error found.

nodes.name: countHop2Brokers
nodes.summary: Counts how many configured brokers use auth.mode: oauth, used to size Hop-2 OAuth validation.

nodes.name: applyToolAuthorizationDefaults
nodes.summary: Synthesizes a default tool_authorization block when OAuth mode is active but the operator omitted one, and defaults GroupsClaimName to "groups".

nodes.name: validateToolAuthorization
nodes.summary: Validates the tool_authorization block: mode compatibility, non-blank groups_claim_name, non-empty access_level_groups, and clean group/tool names.

nodes.name: validateHop1Hop2Alignment
nodes.summary: Validates that Hop 1 (client auth) and Hop 2 (broker OAuth) mode configuration are mutually consistent.

nodes.name: validateBroker
nodes.summary: Validates a single BrokerConfig's URL, auth mode, and credential fields, applying stricter HTTPS/TLS rules in production mode.

nodes.name: validateBrokerOAuthConfig

nodes.summary: Interface describing the token cache contract (Get, Put, Delete, Close) implemented by the Otter-backed cache and consumed by the OAuth token exchanger.

nodes.summary: Pulls the raw subject token out of the request context, exchanges it for a broker access token, and sets the outbound Authorization Bearer header.

nodes.name: circuitbreaker.go
nodes.summary: Configures the gobreaker-based circuit breaker that protects the OAuth token-exchange call to the IdP, classifying errors into success/failure/excluded and logging state transitions.

nodes.name: circuitbreaker_exchange_test.go
nodes.summary: Integration tests exercising the circuit breaker through the full Exchange() call path, covering trip/recovery, half-open probe budgets, singleflight interaction, and concurrent stampede behavior.

nodes.name: circuitbreaker_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the circuit breaker's classification helpers (isBreakerFailure, isBreakerExcluded, isBreakerSuccess) and its ready-to-trip and counting-success factories.

nodes.name: dedup_key.go
nodes.summary: Computes a SHA-256 deduplication key from subject token, broker alias, and audience so identical in-flight token-exchange requests can be collapsed via singleflight.

nodes.name: dedup_key_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests verifying the deduplication key is deterministic, sensitive to each input field, collision-resistant across NUL boundaries, and rendered as lowercase hex.

nodes.name: defaults.go
nodes.summary: Computes the overall chain deadline for a token-exchange retry sequence from an operator override or from per-attempt timeout, max retry wait, and max retry count.

nodes.name: errors.go
nodes.summary: Defines ExchangeError, the structured error type returned by token exchange, including a caller-safe agent-facing message and secure slog attributes for observability.

nodes.name: exchange.go
nodes.summary: Implements the core RFC 8693 token-exchange flow: cache lookup, singleflight-protected exchange with panic recovery, circuit-breaker/retry-after gating, retry classification, and cache invalidation.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines singleflight.Group with a deferred panic-recovery closure so a panicking exchange still surfaces as an error to all waiting callers instead of crashing the goroutine.

nodes.name: exchange_test.go
nodes.summary: Extensive test suite for Exchange(), covering the happy path, singleflight dedup and cancellation-boundary semantics, cache hit/miss/invalidate, retry exhaustion, and structured logging behavior.

nodes.name: newTokenExchangeCircuitBreaker
nodes.summary: Builds a gobreaker.CircuitBreaker configured with the token-exchange ready-to-trip, success-counting, and state-change-logging callbacks.

nodes.name: newReadyToTrip
nodes.summary: Returns the breaker's ReadyToTrip predicate, tripping on a consecutive-failure streak or on the configured failure-rate threshold.

nodes.name: newCountingIsBreakerSuccess
nodes.summary: Wraps isBreakerSuccess to also maintain the atomic consecutive-failure counter used by the ready-to-trip streak check.

nodes.name: isBreakerExcluded
nodes.summary: Determines whether an error class (context cancellation, rate limit, request-build/config fault) should be excluded from circuit-breaker accounting entirely.

nodes.name: isBreakerFailure
nodes.summary: Reports whether an error should count as a circuit-breaker failure, i.e. it is neither excluded nor a success.

nodes.name: DeduplicationKeyInput
nodes.summary: Holds the subject token, broker alias, and audience used to derive a singleflight deduplication key, with String/GoString/LogValue implementations that redact the token.

nodes.name: computeDeduplicationKey
nodes.summary: Hashes the NUL-separated subject token, broker alias, and audience with SHA-256 to produce the singleflight/cache dedup key.

nodes.name: ComputeChainDeadline
nodes.summary: Derives the overall retry-chain deadline for a token exchange from an explicit override or from per-attempt timeout, max retry wait, and max retry count.

nodes.name: ExchangeError
nodes.summary: Structured error returned by token exchange, carrying the token endpoint, broker alias, audience, HTTP status, failure class, and elapsed time, with a caller-safe agent message and slog attributes.

nodes.name: AgentMessage
nodes.summary: Builds a broker-scoped, credential-free error message intended for exposure to the calling MCP agent.

nodes.name: LogAttrs
nodes.summary: Assembles the slog attribute list for an ExchangeError, including failure class, HTTP status, and elapsed duration, without leaking the subject token.

nodes.name: Exchange
nodes.summary: Public entry point for token exchange: checks the token cache, deduplicates concurrent identical requests via singleflight with panic recovery, and handles caller cancellation vs. detached completion.

nodes.name: runProtectedExchange
nodes.summary: Runs one exchange attempt through the Retry-After gate and circuit breaker, or bypasses the breaker entirely when it is disabled.

nodes.name: runExchangeOnce
nodes.summary: Executes a single IdP exchange attempt with a bounded chain-deadline context, classifies the retry outcome, raises the Retry-After gate on exhaustion, and caches successful tokens.

nodes.name: mapCircuitOpen
nodes.summary: Translates the underlying gobreaker open/too-many-requests errors into the package's ExchangeError sentinel for a consistent caller-facing error surface.

nodes.name: Invalidate
nodes.summary: Removes a cached token for the given input's dedup key, forcing the next Exchange call to fetch a fresh token from the IdP.

nodes.name: classifyRetryOutcome
nodes.summary: Determines whether a failed exchange attempt was context-cancelled, hit the retry chain deadline mid-flight, or genuinely exhausted retries, rewrapping the error accordingly and logging the outcome.

nodes.name: doExchange
nodes.summary: Performs the actual HTTP round trip to the IdP token endpoint for one attempt, building the request, sending it, and parsing the response into a Token.

nodes.name: exchanger.go
nodes.summary: Defines the Exchanger struct holding token-exchange configuration and dependencies, and its New() constructor that validates parameters and wires up the circuit breaker and chain deadline.

nodes.name: exchanger_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests for Exchanger's New() constructor, verifying rejection of nil HTTP client/cache, invalid retry-after settings, and correct field copying on success.

nodes.name: request_test.go
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the IdP token-exchange request builder, covering RFC-mandated fields, client auth methods, audience formats, grant-type/auth-method validation, and URL/context handling.

nodes.name: response.go
nodes.summary: Parses IdP token-exchange HTTP responses: decodes success bodies into tokens, classifies OAuth error responses, and extracts/validates Retry-After header values.

nodes.name: response_test.go
nodes.summary: Comprehensive tests for IdP response parsing, covering body-close guarantees, size caps, content-type handling, success/error body decoding, and Retry-After header parsing edge cases.

nodes.name: retry_after_gate.go
nodes.summary: Implements a shared rate-limit gate keyed on a CAS timestamp that blocks new token-exchange attempts until an IdP-issued Retry-After delay (clamped to an operator max) has elapsed.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses atomic CompareAndSwap in a loop so concurrent callers only ever raise the gate, never shorten an already-longer wait.

nodes.name: retry_after_gate_test.go
nodes.summary: Tests for the Retry-After gate covering blocking/unblocking windows, concurrent max-wins semantics, clamping, and the structured log lines emitted when the gate is set, clamped, or skipped.

nodes.name: types.go
nodes.summary: Defines the core token-exchange data types — Params (exchanger configuration), ExchangeInput (per-call request), and Token (result) — with credential-safe String/GoString/LogValue implementations.
nodes.languageNotes: Every type carries a custom LogValue so slog output redacts secrets (client secret, subject token) even if logged via %v or a generic struct dump.

nodes.name: manager.go
nodes.summary: Implements ToolManager, the MCP server's tool registry and dispatcher: routes tool calls to registered handlers, strips the injected broker parameter, validates params/output, and logs structured, security-scrubbed results.
nodes.languageNotes: A deferred closure distinguishes a handler panic from a normal error/success return so panics are always audited as errors rather than silently logged as success.

nodes.name: Exchanger
nodes.summary: The concrete implementation of token exchange: holds IdP endpoint/client config, the HTTP client, token cache, singleflight group, circuit breaker, and Retry-After gate state.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: Constructs an Exchanger from Params, validating required fields, building the circuit breaker, and computing the retry chain deadline.

nodes.name: parseIdPResponse
nodes.summary: Reads and closes the IdP HTTP response body, dispatching to success or error-body parsing based on status code and content type, and extracting any Retry-After header.

nodes.name: parseSuccessBody
nodes.summary: Decodes a 2xx token-exchange response body into a Token, validating the token type, issued-token-type, and expiry, and computing an absolute ExpiresAt.

nodes.name: responseMediaType
nodes.summary: Extracts and normalizes the base media type from a response's Content-Type header, ignoring parameters like charset.

nodes.name: parseRetryAfter
nodes.summary: Parses a Retry-After header (delay-seconds or HTTP-date form) into a duration, preserving the raw header value for logging when parsing fails.

nodes.name: classifyClientError
nodes.summary: Parses a 4xx IdP error body into an OAuth error code/description, falling back to a raw-body message when the body isn't valid OAuth JSON.

nodes.name: clampRetryAfter
nodes.summary: Caps an IdP-requested Retry-After delay at the operator-configured maximum honored duration.

nodes.name: raiseGate
nodes.summary: Atomically raises the shared gated-until timestamp via compare-and-swap, ensuring concurrent callers can only extend, never shorten, the block window.

nodes.name: raiseGateOnExhaustedRateLimit
nodes.summary: Inspects an exhausted-retry error for a rate-limit sentinel and Retry-After value, clamps it, and raises the gate so subsequent attempts fail fast until it elapses.

nodes.name: logGateNotSet
nodes.summary: Logs why the Retry-After gate was not set — either no header was present or its value could not be parsed.

nodes.name: ExchangeInput
nodes.summary: Per-call token-exchange request: subject token, broker alias, and audience, with a DedupKeyInput() adapter and secret-safe logging.

nodes.name: Token
nodes.summary: Result of a successful token exchange: the token value and its absolute expiry, with a LogValue that omits the raw token.

nodes.name: fieldPropertiesSchema

nodes.name: withRecovery
nodes.summary: Wraps an SDK tool handler so a panic inside it becomes a sanitized error result instead of crashing the process, and stamps the correlation ID onto the result on every exit path.

nodes.name: stampCorrelationID

nodes.name: RegisterWithServer

nodes.name: toMCPAnnotations

nodes.name: injectBrokerParam

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build that compiles the solace-broker-mcp Go binary in a golang:1.25-alpine builder stage, then packages it into a minimal distroless nonroot runtime image with bundled license/NOTICE files, a health check, and port 9090 exposed.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build separates build-time Go toolchain dependencies from the runtime image; the runtime stage uses a distroless nonroot base to minimize attack surface, and explicitly copies LICENSE/NOTICE/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md to satisfy Apache-2.0 section 4(d) attribution requirements for a distributed derivative work.

nodes.name: build-and-test.yml
nodes.summary: Required-check CI workflow running lint, build, vet, coverage-gated tests, an informational benchmark, and five Dockerized e2e suites (basic-mcp, oauth, monitoring, management, action) against real Solace brokers; triggered on push to main, opened/synchronized PRs against main, manual dispatch, and as a reusable workflow called by release.yml on tag push.
nodes.languageNotes: Per-commit-SHA concurrency grouping (not per-ref) is deliberate so every push to main keeps its own FOSSA/e2e verdict instead of a burst of merges silently dropping the middle commit's results.

nodes.name: build-image.yaml
nodes.summary: Reusable workflow that builds the Docker image single-arch, scoped to contents:read only, and saves it as a tar artifact for a downstream scan job to load; it never pushes to a registry, keeping the scan path's permission ceiling minimal for every caller.

nodes.name: ci-pr.yaml
nodes.summary: Required pull-request checks for compliance hygiene: routable commit identity (DCO-adjacent), a release-notes extraction self-test, third-party license currency, Apache-2.0 license-header presence, and an advisory CHANGELOG-updated gate. Supply-chain and container scanning were moved out to guardian-scan.yaml.
nodes.languageNotes: Every check runs its own self-test step first, on the principle that a vacuous pass (a check that always goes green) is the more dangerous failure mode than a false alarm.

nodes.name: guardian-scan.yaml
nodes.summary: FOSSA license/vulnerability scanning plus a Prisma Cloud container scan, both reporting to Guardian. Runs report-only on pull requests and enforces a blocking Guardian gate on pushes to main, tags, or a reusable workflow_call; builds its scan image via build-image.yaml. Fork PRs skip scanning entirely since they lack the Environment secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: Convention of computing every derived value once in a `setup` job as string outputs, then mapping each into a job's `env:` block rather than re-interpolating expressions inline, keeps boolean logic auditable via fromJSON() instead of ad hoc string comparisons scattered across jobs.

nodes.name: llm-eval.yml
nodes.summary: Non-gating, time-boxed (2026-08-15 through 2026-09-03) daily-scheduled plus on-demand LLM end-to-end evaluation suite that runs the pinned Claude Code CLI against Dockerized Solace brokers, classifies each run's failure as infrastructure vs. scenario, and uploads a run-record artifact to inform a permanent-vs-on-demand operating-model decision (SOL-153184).
nodes.languageNotes: The schedule trigger is explicitly a dated experiment with a removal deadline written into the workflow comments, guarding against an unowned cron job burning API credits indefinitely.

nodes.name: release-readiness-check.yaml
nodes.summary: Dispatchable and reusable gate that re-runs the Guardian scan in trunk (blocking) mode against a given version/ref before a release is tagged, with an admin-only bypass (skip_security_checks) validated server-side via the GitHub collaborator-permission API rather than trusted from the input.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: Tag-triggered (v*) release pipeline: runs build-and-test, extracts and validates CHANGELOG release notes, verifies third-party license inventories, re-scans via release-readiness, cross-compiles signed/attested binaries for 4 OS/arch combinations, builds and pushes a multi-arch attested Docker image to GHCR, and publishes the GitHub Release with checksums.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately avoids `secrets: inherit` on its reusable-workflow calls, relying on each called workflow's own `environment:` block to resolve secrets, since environment secrets outrank org secrets and inherit would otherwise hand the scan every unrelated org/repo secret.

nodes.name: workflow-lint.yaml
nodes.summary: Required check that lints every workflow under .github/workflows/ with actionlint (correctness plus shellcheck on run: blocks) and zizmor (security posture, offline audits only), both pinned to fixed versions so the gate's verdict cannot move without a commit behind it.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately has no `paths:` filter even though it only concerns workflow files, because GitHub never creates a check run for a filtered-out required context, leaving it pending forever and the PR unmergeable.

nodes.name: .fossa.yml
nodes.summary: FOSSA license-scanning configuration defining the project locator, vendored-dependency scan method, and path exclusions used to generate the third-party license reports.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md

nodes.name: Makefile

nodes.languageNotes: `check` composes build-all, vet, lint, and test-cover to mirror the CI build/lint/test jobs locally; CI is treated as the source of truth if the two drift. Each e2e-*-all target wraps its own up/run/down triplet with teardown guaranteed even on failure.

nodes.name: build-test-licenses-check.sh
nodes.summary: CI compliance gate that verifies THIRD_PARTY_BUILD_TEST.md accurately lists every build/test-time third-party dependency (Go modules, npm packages, GitHub Actions, container images) in both directions, failing when the inventory drifts from what the repository actually uses to build and test itself.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `find -L ... -prune` to discover inputs by walking the filesystem rather than a hardcoded list, deliberately failing closed as the repository grows; every grep is guarded with `|| true` under `set -euo pipefail` to avoid a no-match silently aborting the script.

nodes.summary: CI gate that rejects pull request commits whose author or committer email uses a non-routable domain (.local, .sol-local, .internal, .lan) or a bare hostname, preventing an internal machine identity from being published permanently in public git history.
nodes.languageNotes: Denylist rather than allowlist so outside contributors are never blocked; walks only the commits the PR adds via git rev-list, excluding the live base tip so commits merged to base after the run started are not misattributed.

nodes.name: commit-identity-check.test.sh

nodes.name: extract-release-notes.test.sh

nodes.name: license-header-check.sh

nodes.name: license-header-check.test.sh

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: solace-broker-mcp is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, written in Go, that lets AI assistants like Claude Code monitor and manage Solace event brokers. The README explains the shape of the whole system: 40 tools (24 read-only, 16 gated write/action tools) that translate natural-language requests into calls against the broker's SEMP v1/v2 management APIs, with authentication, rate limiting, retries, and response formatting handled by the server. Keep this tool count and read/write split in mind — it reappears as the organizing idea behind the tool layer covered later in the tour.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: cmd/server/main.go is where the process starts: it loads configuration, wires up the SEMP broker pool and composite tool executor, registers every MCP tool behind authentication/authorization middleware, and runs the HTTP(S) server with graceful shutdown. It also doubles as a `--health-check` CLI subcommand used by the container's HEALTHCHECK probe. With 195 outgoing edges, this file touches nearly every package in the codebase, making it the natural map of the whole system.
tour.languageLesson: Go convention places the composition root in `main()` — it is the one place allowed to know about every package, wiring dependencies together before handing control to long-lived goroutines (the HTTP server) and registering signal handlers for graceful shutdown.

tour.title: Configuration and Defaults
tour.description: internal/config/config.go defines the full ServerConfig schema (brokers, SEMP client settings, two-hop auth, observability) and loads it from YAML with ${VAR} environment substitution and exhaustive validation. It is the single most depended-upon file in the codebase (54 incoming references), because nearly every subsystem needs a piece of this config. internal/defaults/defaults.go complements it by centralizing every default value — ports, timeouts, TLS, OAuth, retry — each documented with the reasoning behind the choice, so operators can see why a default is what it is.
tour.languageLesson: Go structs commonly use field tags (`yaml:"..."`) to drive declarative unmarshaling, keeping the parsing logic separate from the schema definition itself.

tour.title: The Broker Client and Connection Pool
tour.description: Building on the config from Step 3, internal/semp/broker.go constructs a per-broker BrokerClient that bundles SEMPv1 and SEMPv2 HTTP clients, a rate limiter, a shared cookie jar, and the configured authenticator (basic, bearer, or OAuth) for one broker alias. internal/semp/pool.go lazily creates and caches one BrokerClient per configured alias behind a BrokerPool, giving every tool handler concurrency-safe access by name. internal/semp/sempv2/client.go is the concrete SEMPv2 REST client underneath, building authenticated requests and parsing SEMPv2 error responses — this is the layer that actually talks to Solace brokers.
tour.languageLesson: Go interfaces let the same tool-handler code work against either the SEMPv1 (legacy XML) or SEMPv2 (REST/JSON) client without knowing which one it's talking to — the pool decides at construction time.

tour.title: Resilience: Retries, Rate Limiting, Transport
tour.description: Talking to production brokers over a network means handling failure gracefully. internal/semp/resilience/retry.go implements the retry policy — marking requests safe or unsafe to retry and deciding when a failed request should be retried. internal/semp/resilience/ratelimiter.go paces outgoing requests per broker with a simple ticker, and internal/semp/resilience/transport.go tunes the underlying http.Transport's timeouts and connection pool size to match the configured per-broker concurrency cap. Together these three files are the resilience layer that sits underneath the broker client from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Go's context package is the idiomatic way to attach retry markers and deadlines to a request as it flows through layers of client code, without changing every function signature.

tour.title: MCP Tool Registry and Dispatch
tour.description: internal/tools/manager.go implements ToolManager, the registry and dispatcher for all 40 MCP tools: it routes tool calls to handlers, strips the auto-injected `broker` parameter, validates params and output, and logs structured, security-scrubbed results. internal/tools/register.go is where every handler actually gets registered — translating internal types into SDK tool definitions, injecting the broker parameter into every schema, wrapping dispatch with panic recovery and correlation-ID stamping, and gating the 16 write/action tools behind `enable_write_tools`. This is the layer that turns the broker client from Steps 4-5 into something an AI assistant can call by name.
tour.languageLesson: Go often implements a plugin-style registry as a map from name to handler function, built once at startup and consulted on every dispatch — cheap, simple, and easy to audit for what's actually exposed.

tour.title: Composite Tools: YAML-Driven Multi-Step Calls
tour.description: Most of the 40 tools are declared, not coded. internal/composite/loader.go loads and validates composite tool definitions from embedded YAML — checking step structure, fan-out configuration, and result-strategy rules — before they're registered with the MCP server. internal/composite/executor.go then runs those definitions step by step against a SEMP client, handling sequential and fan-out steps, cursor-based pagination, and templated argument resolution. The actual catalog lives in tools.yaml, which declares each composite tool as a multi-step SEMPv2 call sequence — this is the preferred way to add a new tool, reserving native Go handlers for logic YAML can't express.
tour.languageLesson: YAML as a declarative DSL trades code flexibility for auditability: a reviewer can see every SEMP call a tool makes without reading Go control flow, and the embed.go pattern compiles the YAML into the binary at build time via Go's `embed` package.

tour.title: Native Go Tool Handlers
tour.description: Where composite YAML can't express the logic — like parsing legacy SEMPv1 XML — tools are hand-written Go handlers instead. internal/tools/sempv1/brokerstatus/handler.go implements get-broker-status by concurrently fetching version, spool, message-spool, and (on appliances) hardware status and assembling them into one response. internal/tools/sempv1/redundancy/handler.go implements get-redundancy-status by issuing a SEMPv1 `show redundancy` command and parsing the result. These sit alongside the composite tools from Step 7 as the two mechanisms for adding a tool, chosen based on whether the logic fits YAML.
tour.languageLesson: Go's `encoding/xml` package unmarshals SEMPv1's legacy XML responses into typed structs, the same way `encoding/json` handles SEMPv2 — the parsing model differs but the handler pattern stays consistent.

tour.title: Client Authentication and Authorization
tour.description: Before a tool call ever reaches the registry from Step 6, it passes through authentication. internal/auth/middleware.go builds the Hop 1 (MCP client) authentication middleware — selecting disabled, static-token, or OIDC/JWT verification based on config, and extracting token claims. internal/authz/authz.go then compiles the admin's tool-authorization config into an index and decides whether a caller's claimed groups authorize a specific tool call. internal/semp/auth/oauth.go handles Hop 2 — exchanging the inbound client's subject token for a broker-scoped access token before the request reaches the broker client from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Go HTTP middleware is typically a function that wraps an http.Handler with another http.Handler, letting auth, recovery, and correlation concerns compose as layered wrappers around the same request.

tour.title: OAuth Token Exchange and Identity Provider Integration
tour.description: The Hop 2 OAuth flow from Step 9 relies on internal/tokenexchange/exchange.go, which implements the core RFC 8693 token-exchange flow: cache lookup, singleflight-protected exchange, circuit-breaker and retry-after gating, and cache invalidation on failure. internal/idpclient/client.go builds the hardened HTTP client used to actually talk to the identity provider, with an optional custom CA pool configured via functional options. internal/config/idp_circuit_breaker.go validates the operator-facing circuit-breaker settings — one of the highest fan-in files in the codebase, since the breaker configuration is threaded through the entire token-exchange subsystem.
tour.languageLesson: The functional-options pattern (`WithTimeout(...)`, `WithCACert(...)`) is idiomatic Go for constructors with many optional parameters, avoiding both long positional argument lists and a proliferation of constructor variants.

tour.title: Observability: Correlation, Health, and Log Sanitization
tour.description: Every request flowing through the layers above is traced and logged safely. internal/observability/correlation/correlation.go gates correlation-ID propagation so requests can be traced across the auth, tool-dispatch, and broker layers. internal/observability/health/health.go serves the /livez and legacy /health probes that the Kubernetes deployment (covered later) relies on for liveness checks. internal/observability/logging/sanitize/sanitize.go is the last line of defense against log-injection attacks — its Claim function strips control and bidirectional-override characters from admin- or IdP-controlled strings before they reach a log line, closing off CWE-117 and CWE-1007.
tour.languageLesson: Sanitizing untrusted strings before logging is a defense specific to structured logging pipelines: a malicious control character or bidi-override in a claim value can forge or hide log lines if it reaches the sink unescaped.

tour.title: The Tool Catalog, Documented
tour.description: docs/tools-reference.md is the exhaustive per-tool reference for everything built in Steps 6-8 — every one of the 40 MCP tools, grouped by domain (broker status, queues, VPNs, replication, Kafka, and more), documenting the auto-injected `broker` parameter from Step 6, pagination conventions from the composite executor in Step 7, and the write-tool gating introduced in Step 6. Where the README in Step 1 gave the high-level pitch, this document is the ground truth an operator or AI assistant consults for exact tool behavior.

tour.title: Containerization and Kubernetes Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages everything from Steps 2-11 into a production image using a multi-stage build: the builder stage (golang:1.25-alpine) compiles the binary from cmd/server with CGO disabled, while the runtime stage copies only the compiled binary and license notices into a minimal distroless nonroot image, exposing port 9090 with a health check that calls the `--health-check` subcommand from Step 2. deploy/kubernetes/deployment.yaml and service.yaml then run that image in a cluster, tuning startup/liveness/readiness probes around a 45-second termination grace period so in-flight requests can drain during the graceful shutdown built into main.go.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds separate compile-time dependencies (the Go toolchain, module cache) from the runtime image, so the final container only ships what's needed to run the binary — here, a distroless base with no shell, package manager, or Go toolchain, shrinking the attack surface as well as the image size.

tour.title: CI/CD: Build, Test, and Release
tour.description: pipeline:.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml is the required CI check: it runs lint, build, vet, coverage-gated unit tests, and five Dockerized end-to-end suites against real Solace brokers, triggered on every PR and reused by the release workflow on tag push. The Makefile mirrors this locally with 34 targets — `make check` runs the same build/lint/test steps CI does, and dedicated targets bring up, run, and tear down each Dockerized e2e suite. This is the capstone: the same containerized artifact built in Step 13 is what gets tested here before every release.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows are structured around `on` triggers, `jobs` that can run in parallel, and `steps` within a job that run sequentially — a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`) lets the release pipeline invoke this same test suite rather than duplicating it.
